subject: botany_2
question_text: Explain the reactions of Krebs cycle.

mark_split.label: What the Krebs cycle is, and where

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.12, printed question 2. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Two spelling slips corrected on this card: the guide prints "Fumerase" for FUMARASE and "Fumeric acid" and "FAD⁺" in its p.13 diagram for fumaric acid and FAD. The guide's mnemonic is printed partly in Telugu script; the product is English-only (Rule 30i), so a plain English memory device is given instead. Figure revision (figure audit, 2026-09-05): the citric acid label and leader moved to the upper left, so the leader runs from its own label to the ring and no longer crosses the acetyl CoA arrow.

insider_note: Ten steps, but only four of them are the ones examiners check: the three oxidations that make NADH, and the one that makes FADH2. Get the tally right and the answer holds together even if a step name slips.

steps.label: What the Krebs cycle is, and where
steps.margin_note: Definition, site, what is oxidised, and the three names of the cycle.
lines: The KREBS CYCLE is a cyclic series of reactions
that occurs in ALL AEROBIC organisms.
It takes place in the MATRIX of the
In it, acetyl coenzyme A is completely oxidised
ADP is converted into energy-rich ATP.
It is also called the citric acid cycle or the
steps.why: It is a cycle because the compound it ends by making, oxaloacetic acid, is the one it began by using — so the pathway can run again without any new acceptor.
common_mistakes: Saying the Krebs cycle occurs in the cytoplasm. That is glycolysis; Krebs is in the mitochondrial MATRIX.
Calling it partial oxidation. The Krebs cycle COMPLETELY oxidises acetyl CoA.
Saying it happens in anaerobic respiration. It needs oxygen.
steps.memory_tip: Mitochondrial matrix, complete oxidation, and it ends where it began.

steps.label: The link reaction
steps.margin_note: Name it, give the equation, and say it is NOT part of the cycle. That last point is the mark.
lines: Pyruvic acid from glycolysis enters the
This is the LINK REACTION, joining glycolysis
It is not part of the cycle itself.
steps.why: The cycle can only accept a two-carbon acetyl group, so the three-carbon pyruvate must lose one carbon before it can enter — which is what the link reaction does.
common_mistakes: Counting the link reaction as the first step of the cycle. It is a separate step BEFORE it.
Forgetting the CO2. One carbon is lost here, which is how 3C becomes 2C.
Saying pyruvate enters the cycle directly. It enters as ACETYL CoA.
steps.memory_tip: Three carbons in, two carbons on: one is lost before the cycle starts.

steps.label: Steps 1-5
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Number every step, name the reaction TYPE and the enzyme. The reaction types are what make the ten steps memorable.
steps.why: The first five steps turn a six-carbon acid into a five-carbon one, so the carbon that entered as acetyl has already begun leaving as carbon dioxide.
common_mistakes: Naming the first enzyme 'citric acid'. The enzyme is CITRATE SYNTHASE.
Missing that aconitase catalyses steps 2 AND 3. The same enzyme does both.
Forgetting the first NADH. Step 4 is the first of three oxidations.
steps.memory_tip: Condense to six carbons, then lose the first carbon dioxide at step 5.

steps.label: Steps 6-10
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Step 8 with FAD and step 10 closing the cycle are the two an examiner looks for.
steps.why: Step 10 regenerates oxaloacetic acid, the very compound step 1 used, and that is what closes the cycle and lets it run again.
common_mistakes: Writing 'fumerase'. The enzyme is FUMARASE. The guide misprints it.
Saying step 8 reduces NAD+. Step 8 is the ONE step that reduces FAD, not NAD+.
Not saying that step 10 regenerates oxaloacetic acid. That is what makes it a cycle.
steps.memory_tip: Three steps reduce NAD, one reduces FAD, one makes ATP.

steps.label: Diagram — the Krebs cycle
steps.margin_note: No diagram mark — the question says 'explain the reactions'. Drawing it is still the quickest way to check the tally in the final step.

elements.caption: Step 1 — pyruvate enters as acetyl coenzyme A
Step 3 — the eight acids of the cycle
Step 4 — the tally for one turn, and the names

steps.why: Drawn as a ring, the eight acids can be seen returning to the one they started from, and the per-turn tally written inside is the same tally the last written step is marked on.
common_mistakes: Drawing acetyl CoA joining anything other than oxaloacetic acid. Step 1 is acetyl CoA PLUS oxaloacetic acid.
Drawing three carbon dioxide molecules leaving the cycle. Only TWO leave the cycle; the third came from the link reaction, outside it.
Drawing the ring anticlockwise. The order citric, isocitric, α-KG, succinyl CoA, succinic, fumaric, malic, oxaloacetic runs CLOCKWISE here.
steps.memory_tip: Eight acids round, back to where it started: two CO2, three NADH, one FADH2, one ATP.

steps.label: The yield per turn
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Give the per-turn figures, then double them for one glucose. Naming which step each product came from is what separates a full answer from a memorised list.

lines.text: Per turn: 2 CO2, 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, 1 ATP

lines: Each turn of the cycle gives:
One glucose gives TWO acetyl CoA, so the cycle
turns TWICE per glucose, and every figure above
steps.why: The reduced coenzymes are the real product: they carry their electrons to the electron transport chain, where most of the ATP is actually made.
common_mistakes: Giving the yield per glucose as if it were per turn. The cycle turns TWICE per glucose.
Counting the link reaction's NADH as one of the three. The three come from steps 4, 6 and 10.
Saying the Krebs cycle makes most of the ATP directly. It makes only ONE ATP per turn; the NADH and FADH2 do the rest, later.
steps.memory_tip: Two out as gas, four as reduced coenzymes, one as ATP.
